NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 28, 10:04 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 19.7 DraftKings points for $7,400, at Dallas. Brock Bowers (14.0, $7,600) and Sam LaPorta (12.7, $5,100) are next.

Trey McBride is also the top value at the position: 2.67 projected points per $1,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 28, 10:04 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 8

Trey McBride, ARI at DAL ($7,400)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 19.7 DraftKings points at $7,400. That is 5.8 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 10.9 targets on 39.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.67 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 19.8 points with a simulated floor of 5.0 and a ceiling of 48.3, and he holds 19% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 6-point underdog on the road against Dallas, with an implied team total of 24.25 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at NYJ ($7,600)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 14.0 DraftKings points at $7,600. The model gives him 7.6 targets on 32.0 routes. The salary works out to 1.84 projected points per $1,000, 16th of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 13.9 points with a simulated floor of 2.2 and a ceiling of 36.9, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 1.5-point underdog on the road against the Jets, with an implied team total of 22 in a game totaled at 45.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs NE ($3,200)

Greg Dulcich projects for 8.2 DraftKings points at $3,200, which works out to 2.57 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 17 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.2 targets on 17.8 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 8.3 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 33.1, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7.5-point underdog at home against New England, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.
